finding: Spring 2026 statewide initiatives paid circulators up to $15 per signature (NYT via Ballot Access News, SF Examiner), with some $7-12. Per an unverified commenter, local petitions paid $20+ and coordinators received $30+ per signature on $15 petitions. One unverified commenter estimated about $125M spent across 9 CA initiatives (~$10 per raw signature). A video of $5-per-signature payments to signers on a billionaire-tax counter-measure triggered a state probe.

Ballotpedia put the 2024 national average at nearly $15 per signature. 2024 average cost per required signature (CPRS) by firm: AMT $24.37, Landslide $24.17, Blitz $20.86, FieldWorks $19.01, PCI $30.85, The Outreach Team $32.16, Victors $10.87, and Washington firms as low as $4.51.

topic: Hourly pay in states that ban per-signature pay
finding: Current postings run $20-50/hr. Most Outreach Team and PS Logistics roles pay $20-27/hr, LMK Strategies in Dallas pays $34-50/hr, and Arizona 2024 rates ran $25-30/hr, with Petition Partners top workers at about $55/hr.

There are 9 questions on the Nov 2026 ballot, tied for the most ever. A referendum petition on the Aug 10, 2026 abortion law (Mass. Citizens for Life / Mass. Family Action) is live now: signatures were due to local clerks Oct 23 and are due to the Secretary of State Nov 6. It needs 37,289 signatures for the 2028 ballot and 49,719 to suspend the law. Harold Hubschman filed 10 prospective 2028 questions. A pending bill would ban per-signature pay and require a paid-circulator disclosure. The Aug 2025 filing produced 42 laws for 2026 and 5 constitutional amendments for 2028. By analogy, the 2028 statute cycle should start with filings in Aug 2027 (inference, not verified).

Initiatives to the legislature need 308,911 valid signatures; the state recommends submitting about 390,000. The last cycle's deadline was Jan 2, 2026. Let's Go Washington was weighing the 2026 ballot versus an initiative to the legislature (for 2027) to repeal the 9.9% millionaires' income tax (May 2026). Whether it chose the initiative-to-the-legislature route was not verified. The 'initiative killer' restriction bill died in the legislature in Feb 2026. FieldWorks' Nov 25 - Dec 4 travel crew fits a late-year WA push, but this is unconfirmed.
The 2026 initiative filing deadline was Feb 2, 2026, requiring 67,682 signatures. The next cycle's requirement and deadline were not verified this session.

Circulators must be Florida residents and U.S. citizens and must register with the Division of Elections. Felons without restored rights are barred. Organizations face fines up to $50,000 per ineligible circulator, petitions must be turned in within 10 days (down from 30), and filling in missing petition information is a third-degree felony. A July 2025 preliminary ruling was mixed: some non-citizen/non-resident provisions were enjoined per the Floridian Press headline. After a Feb 2026 trial, Judge Mark Walker upheld the law around Apr 30, 2026. Florida Decides Healthcare was considering an appeal and relaunched for 2028. The net effect is to shut out the out-of-state traveling-circulator model and favor local, Florida-resident crews.

SB 102 bans per-signature pay, requires State Police background checks for paid canvassers, expands disqualifying offenses, and requires local canvassers to be U.S. citizens and Arkansas residents. SB 207 requires a verbal or written fraud warning to signers (Class A misdemeanor if skipped). HB 1221 makes signatures expire at the next general election. HB 1222 expands the AG's power to reject measures. All were signed Mar 3, 2025.

21 of 26 initiative states have at least one circulator requirement: 10 ban per-signature pay, 6 require residency, 9 require citizenship, and 12 require paid/volunteer disclosure. Arkansas, Florida, Oklahoma and Montana adopted new circulator policies in 2025, and no state adopted one in 2026. FL and OK have rules in all five areas, while MA, MD, MO, OH and WA have none.

South Dakota's HB 1087 (a total ban on paid circulators) failed in the House in Jan 2026 over First Amendment concerns (Meyer v. Grant, 1988). The Michigan Senate passed a per-signature pay ban (SB 529 et al.) on Nov 13, 2025, but its fate in the GOP House was uncertain and no enactment was found. Massachusetts has a pending per-signature ban bill. Montana's CI-133, on the Nov 2026 ballot, aims to shield the initiative process from government interference (article not fetched). Utah and Missouri 2025-26 changes were not verified because the search budget ran out.

AMT v. Let the Voters Decide et al. (worker-poaching, W.D. Mo., Nov 2025) and the Missouri AG probe of AMT. Michigan voters report misrepresentation by gatherers. California has the $5-per-signer video probe. Quality control and compliance are becoming selling points with clients.

Municipal drives are active: Nashville fairgrounds referendum, Wisconsin and Michigan city healthcare-committee measures (City Action Michigan; Kalamazoo measure on the Nov 2026 ballot), 4 Dallas drives (Oct 2026, details not retrieved), and Colorado's 75 licensed 2026 petition entities. This supports a local-campaign niche.
